title: Actionable alert — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, an alert has no owner or runbook. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences on what makes an alert actionable, what this one lacks, and the first thing you would add.

vocabulary.meaning: the discipline of firing only on conditions someone can act on, since an alert nobody acts on trains the team to ignore alerts
the short procedure attached to an alert, telling the person woken up what to check and what to do first

expectedElements: The absence of an owner is treated as a defect
The cost of unactionable alerts is named
One concrete first addition is proposed
modelAnswer: The alert lacks an owner and a runbook, which are the two conditions that make it actionable. Without an owner it fires into a shared channel and responsibility diffuses; without a runbook whoever responds has to rediscover what to check under time pressure. The real cost is cumulative: alerts nobody can act on train the team to ignore alerts generally, including the ones that matter. I would add a three-line runbook first, since it converts the signal into an action and tells the responder which evidence to collect.
commonMistakes: Treating the missing owner as an administrative detail
Proposing to tune the threshold instead of making the alert actionable
variants: Rewrite the update as the three-line runbook itself.
